subject: FintechCo - API auth & key management follow-up

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: FintechCo - API auth & key management follow-up

Thanks again for taking the time today, Alex - great conversation. Quick recap and the items we promised to follow up on from the discovery call:

Summary:
- FintechCo is evaluating Redwood for production inference (text generation + embeddings + reranker).
- Primary auth preference: service-account-based access for server-to-server integrations; security team prefers short-lived creds and centralized KMS.
- Compliance requirements: audit logs retained 12 months, key rotation cadence (TBD), RBAC for API key issuance, and visibility into token usage per environment.

Questions / items we promised to clarify (see inline):
1) Supported auth modes: Hosted API vs Private (VPC) differences - we’ll outline options below.
2) Key rotation patterns and automation (we’ll propose a flow + sample code).
3) Scoping of keys for embeddings/rerankers and structured output/tool calling.
4) Network/IP allowlist and audit log details.

Attachments: redwood-kms-integration-guide.pdf (high level: hosted vs private KMS options + rotation patterns).

Short answers (high-level):
- Redwood supports API keys (long-lived) and OAuth/JWT-style short-lived tokens. For customers wanting customer-managed KMS and full control, Private deployment (or Dedicated with KMS integration) is the recommended path. Hosted API supports per-service-account API keys with envelope encryption and rotation hooks.
- We can scope keys by route (read-only embeddings vs generation) and by allowed model set. Embeddings API keys can be scoped to embedding-only and rate/usage limits applied.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm which GCP project(s) FintechCo plans to use for KMS and whether you want Redwood to integrate with your KMS or use Redwood-managed keys?
- Can you share the list of public egress IPs (or confirm you’ll use VPC peering) so we can validate networking requirements?
- We’ll schedule a technical deep dive next week with your infra/security folks (Dev/infra deep dive, 60m).

I’m looping in Dev (cc) to propose the technical options and a short SDK example for token rotation.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa - appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side to help the technical dive:

Auth setup at FintechCo (current):
- Primary identity is Google Cloud service accounts. We prefer short-lived JWTs minted per service account, exchanged for platform tokens.
- KMS: Google Cloud KMS (projects: fintechco-main / fintechco-prod); we prefer Redwood to integrate with our KMS if possible.
- Key rotation: target cadence is 60-90 days for long-lived keys; for short-lived tokens we want automatic rotation and auditability.
- Audit: must produce per-token logs and token->request mapping; SOC2 compliance team needs consistent retention for logs.

Network / security:
- We will provide egress IP ranges for the infra team. We prefer VPC peering for Prod if supported.

Scoping & use cases:
- We want separate creds for embedding/reranking workloads (higher QPS from vector pipeline) vs. generation (latency-sensitive).
- For tool-calling/structured output, we'd like scoping that restricts action-capable tokens (only certain service accounts can call external tools).

Attached is our internal requirements spreadsheet: fintechco-authn-requirements.xlsx - it has fields for rotation windows, logging retention, KMS project IDs, and current allowed IP ranges.

Two technical questions for Dev (cc):
1) Does Redwood support JWKS/OAuth with automatic discovery endpoints (we’d like to use standard OIDC flows for service accounts)?
2) For Hosted API, how do you recommend handling short-lived tokens vs. API keys for CI/CD jobs that need non-interactive access?

Thanks - happy to meet next week.

Alex Johnson
Head of Infra | FintechCo

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: FintechCo - API auth & key management follow-up

Hi Alex - quick technical responses and recommended patterns. TL;DR: we support both JWKS/OIDC and API-key flows; recommend short-lived tokens for service-to-service (mint + exchange) and scoped API keys for CI/CD where rotation automation is harder.

1) JWKS / OIDC support:
- Hosted API: We support verifying inbound JWTs against customer JWKS (OIDC discovery) and map claims to Redwood scopes. This allows FintechCo to mint short-lived JWTs (using your service account) and send them directly to Redwood; we validate kid/iss/aud and issue a short-lived Redwood session token if configured.
- Private/Dedicated: full integration with your KMS for signing and key storage is supported.

2) Key rotation patterns:
- Recommended: short-lived tokens (15m-1h) issued by FintechCo's auth broker, exchanged for Redwood session tokens. For long-lived API keys, use envelope encryption with customer-wrapped keys in GCP KMS and implement rotation by creating a new key version + updating the wrapped key on our side.
- We provide webhooks for key-rotation events and an API to revoke keys immediately.

3) Scoping tokens by capability:
- We can scope tokens at the route level (embeddings-only, generation-only), by model families, and by features (tool-calling/structured-output enabled or disabled).
- For tool-calling, we support an allowlist of action-capable service accounts. Tokens without that flag cannot trigger tool calls.

4) Audit logs and token -> request mapping:
- Hosted: we surface per-token, per-route logs in Redwood Console and can export to your GCS/S3 for retention. Logs include token_id, issuing_service_account (if provided), request_id, and model. Retention/export policies configurable.

5) Networking:
- Hosted: allowlist via known Redwood egress IPs (we'll provide the list) or use VPC peering / PrivateLink for Dedicated/Private.

Sample Node snippet (mint + exchange flow):
```js
// FintechCo: mint signed JWT with your SA, exchange for Redwood token
const jwt = mintSignedJwt(serviceAccountKey, {aud: 'https://api.redwoodinference.com/token-exchange', exp: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + 300});
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/token-exchange', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
  body: JSON.stringify({assertion: jwt})
});
const {redwood_token} = await res.json();
// Use redwood_token in Authorization: Bearer <redwood_token> for subsequent calls
```

API-key rotation webhook (example):
- POST /v1/keys/:key_id/rotate triggers immediate re-wrap and notifies your system with old_key_id -> new_key_id mapping.

Action items I recommend off the call (mutual action plan):
- FintechCo: confirm KMS project IDs, provide allowed egress IPs or confirm VPC peering intent. (Owner: Alex)
- Redwood (Dev/Marissa): produce a short implementation guide for token exchange + sample code (Owner: Dev)

If helpful, I can run a short 60m technical deep dive with your infra team to walk the token-exchange flow and show the console logs.
